definitions.explanation: The act of drinking a beverage quickly, whether in a competitive context, out of hurry, or as a social activity. Can refer to both alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks.

examples.japanese: ビールの{早飲|はやの}み{競争|きょうそう}をした。
{早飲|はやの}みは{体|からだ}に{良|よ}くないから{気|き}をつけて。
examples.english: Drinking too fast isn't good for your body, so be careful.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}は{時間|じかん}がないので、コーヒーを{早飲|はやの}みして{出|で}かける。
examples.english: I don't have time in the morning, so I quickly drink my coffee and head out.

notes:
Composed of {早|はや} (fast, quick) and {飲|の}み (drinking), the noun form of {飲|の}む (to drink). Part of the productive {早|はや}+verb stem pattern: {早食|はやぐ}い (eating fast), {早起|はやお}き (getting up early), {早歩|はやある}き (walking fast), etc.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {早飲|はやの}み{競争|きょうそう}: speed-drinking contest
- {早飲|はやの}み{早食|はやぐ}い: eating and drinking fast
- {早飲|はやの}みする: to drink quickly

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {一気飲|いっきの}み: chugging all at once — drinking an entire drink in one go, often used in party contexts
- {早食|はやぐ}い: fast eating — the eating counterpart; also considered unhealthy
- {飲|の}み{干|ほ}す: to drink up — to drain a glass completely
